title: Exploded View
summary: A Claude Code plugin that maps a codebase or an agent harness into an interactive HTML diagram. A Python engine clones, scans, merges, and renders, while the user's own Claude Code session and its subagents write the map itself.

nodes.label: User
nodes.summary: Runs `/exploded-view:map` on a GitHub URL or a local folder, then reads the map in a browser.

nodes.label: Map skill
nodes.summary: The instructions Claude Code loads for the command: prepare, write the top level, dispatch drill-ins, merge.
nodes.details:
- Holds the context-discipline rule: the main session reads only the overview prompt, a few repo files, and short engine output.
- Names the engine with `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`, which Claude Code substitutes when it loads the skill.
- Points to a troubleshooting reference read only when a step fails.

nodes.label: Main session
nodes.summary: The user's Claude Code session: reads the digest and key files, writes the top level, coordinates drill-ins.

nodes.label: Drill-in writers
nodes.summary: One subagent per large part, run in parallel; each reads its scope and writes that part's inside.
nodes.details: Each writer gets a prompt file with the rules, the schema, its place in the map, its siblings, and a digest limited to its scope. It may nest small sub-parts directly and give big ones a scope for the next wave. It replies with one line.

nodes.label: Engine
nodes.summary: Stdlib Python script that resolves, scans, writes prompts, checks parts, merges, sanitises, and renders.

nodes.label: Target resolver
nodes.summary: Turns a URL, owner/repo, or path into a folder to scan, cloning remote repos into a cache.
nodes.details: GitHub `/tree/<branch>/<folder>` links are split against the remote's real refs. HTTPS is tried before SSH, with git prompts turned off, so private repos use the user's existing credentials.

nodes.label: Scanner
nodes.summary: Lists tracked files, pulls one-line summaries, resolves imports and links, and detects harness parts.
nodes.details: Outside-repo config (user-level hooks, untracked MCP config, launchd jobs) is read only for local folders and labelled as this machine's config.

nodes.label: Digest and prompts
nodes.summary: Writes the capped digest and the overview, one-pass, and drill-in prompts with the modelling rules.

nodes.label: Part assembler
nodes.summary: Joins the overview and written parts, lists pending drill-ins, and checks one part against its ancestors.
nodes.details: Parts are cached by commit. `next` caps the run at the agent budget, largest parts first, and gives up on a drill-in after two tries.

nodes.label: Merge and sanitise
nodes.summary: Assembles the final map, strips secrets and local paths, adds source and coverage, and validates.

nodes.label: Renderer
nodes.summary: Inlines the map data and the layout engine into the viewer template to make one HTML file.

nodes.label: Static mapper
nodes.summary: Builds a map from folders, imports, and links alone, for use without any AI.

flows.name: What `prepare` does
flows.summary: From a target string to a ready overview prompt.

steps.text: Recognises the target and clones it if it is remote, recording the commit.
The scanner walks the files git tracks and resolves references between them.
The digest is written with size caps, and the overview prompt wraps it in the rules and schema.

nodes.label: git
nodes.summary: The user's own git, which clones remote repos with whatever credentials already work for them.

nodes.label: Map folder
nodes.summary: `~/exploded-view/<name>/`: job, digest, prompts, parts cached by commit, map.json, and index.html.
nodes.details: Share `index.html`. The working files contain local paths and stay on the machine.

nodes.label: Viewer
nodes.summary: The single-file HTML map: layout, drill-down, workflow playback, details, and search.

nodes.label: Auto layout
nodes.summary: Lays out each level with ELK, trying left-to-right and top-down and keeping the more readable result.

nodes.label: Drill-down navigation
nodes.summary: Opens stacked cards, shows outside neighbours as dashed cards, and keeps the place in the URL.

nodes.label: Workflow player
nodes.summary: Plays a flow hop by hop with numbered badges and a pulse along each connection.

nodes.label: Details and search
nodes.summary: Shows a part's details, connections, and key files (linked to GitHub), and searches every level.

nodes.label: Source section
nodes.summary: Shows where the map came from, the commit, and what a cloned repo could not reveal.

nodes.label: Plugin manifest
nodes.summary: Tells Claude Code the plugin's name and lets users add this repo as a marketplace.

flows.name: Mapping a repo
flows.summary: What happens between typing the command and the map opening.

steps.text: The user runs `/exploded-view:map <target>` and Claude Code loads the skill.
`prepare` resolves the target, clones it if needed, scans it, and writes the overview prompt.
The session reads that prompt and a few key files, writes the top level, and checks it.
For each part `next` lists, a subagent writes its inside; deeper parts follow in the next wave.
`merge` assembles the parts, removes secrets and local paths, validates, and renders.
The single HTML file opens in the browser.

flows.name: Keeping the session's context small
flows.summary: Why a large repo doesn't fill the user's conversation.

steps.text: The digest is capped: content-heavy folders fold into one line, lockfiles drop out, and file and reference lists have limits.
Drill-ins happen in subagents, which reply with one line each.
Only short summaries come back: a pending list, check results, and the merge counts. The merged map is never read back.

flows.name: Re-running on the same commit
flows.summary: How a second run reuses finished work.

steps.text: `prepare` finds the same commit and reports the overview as cached.
Parts live under the commit's folder, so `next` lists only what is still missing.
`merge` renders straight away if nothing is missing.
